NASA is developing the Uranus Orbiter and Probe concept to study Uranus and its moons over a 4.5-year science phase. The mission involves deploying an atmospheric probe into Uranus while conducting multiple flybys of its major moons. But what if a spacecraft skims too close during a atmospheric descent or flyby? Skimming an atmosphere converts kinetic energy into blinding heat, while missing the trajectory leaves it stranded off course in deep space. Would you risk a close flyby?
